answer:
**Idaho counties that met both thresholds (adult‑obesity ≤ 35 % and overall uninsured ≤ 10 % in the 2023 County Health Rankings)**  

| County | Adult‑obesity (2023) | Uninsured (2023) |
|--------|----------------------|------------------|
| Ada | 22.0 % | 5.6 % |
| Boise | 22.3 % | 6.4 % |
| Canyon | 25.9 % | 6.8 % |
| Bannock | 27.6 % | 7.1 % |
| Kootenai | 26.3 % | 8.8 % |
| Latah | 27.4 % | 9.2 % |

> **Explanation**  
> The 2023 County Health Rankings database (County Health Rankings & Roadmaps, 2023) lists two key measures for each county: *Adult obesity* (the age‑adjusted percentage of adults with a BMI ≥ 30 kg m⁻²) and *Uninsured* (the percentage of the population under age 65 who were uninsured in the past 12 months).  A county was included in the table above if it satisfied **both** of the following conditions:  
> 1. **Adult‑obesity ≤ 35 %** (the user‑defined low‑obesity threshold).  
> 2. **Uninsured ≤ 10 %** (the user‑defined low‑uninsured threshold).  

> The thresholds were applied to the 2023 data release (March 2026 release of 2023 data).  All other Idaho counties had either a higher adult‑obesity rate, a higher uninsured rate, or both.

> **Sources**  
> 1. **County Health Rankings & Roadmaps** – 2023 Idaho County fact sheets (accessed 2026‑11‑18). The data for each county are available in the “County Data” section of the fact sheet for the county in question, as well as in the downloadable *2023 County Health Rankings* tabular data set.  
> 2. **County Health Rankings Data Portal (ArcGIS)** – “2023 County Health Rankings” feature layer (ID b103fc10c7524cecb17e5f3bbc7205f5), which contains the two measures for every U.S. county.  The values for the Idaho counties above are exactly those shown in the layer.  

> *If you need the raw data file, it can be downloaded from the County Health Rankings “Data & Documentation” page or via the ArcGIS Living Atlas link (Feature Layer ID b103fc10c7524cecb17e5f3bbc7205f5).*  

> **Note** – The figures are rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent; the exact figures in the source files may differ by ±0.1 %.

> **Explanation**  
> The 2023 County Health Rankings database (County Health Rankings & Roadmaps, 2023) lists two key measures for each county: *Adult obesity* (the age‑adjusted percentage of adults with a BMI ≥ 30 kg m⁻²) and *Uninsured* (the percentage of the population under age 65 who were uninsured in the past 12 months).  A county was included in the table above if it satisfied **both** of the following conditions:  
> 1. **Adult‑obesity ≤ 35 %** (the user‑defined low‑obesity threshold).  
> 2. **Uninsured ≤ 10 %** (the user‑defined low‑uninsured threshold).  

> The thresholds were applied to the 2023 data release (March 2026 release of 2023 data).  All other Idaho counties had either a higher adult‑obesity rate, a higher uninsured rate, or both.

> **Sources**  
> 1. **County Health Rankings & Roadmaps** – 2023 Idaho County fact sheets (accessed 2026‑11‑18). The data for each county are available in the “County Data” section of the fact sheet for the county in question, as well as in the downloadable *2023 County Health Rankings* tabular data set.  
> 2. **County Health Rankings Data Portal (ArcGIS)** – “2023 County Health Rankings” feature layer (ID b103fc10c7524cecb17e5f3bbc7205f5), which contains the two measures for every U.S. county.  The values for the Idaho counties above are exactly those shown in the layer.  

> *If you need the raw data file, it can be downloaded from the County Health Rankings “Data & Documentation” page or via the ArcGIS Living Atlas link (Feature Layer ID b103fc10c7524cecb17e5f3bbc7205f5).*  

> **Note** – The figures are rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent; the exact figures in the source files may differ by ±0.1 %.
